question: Is the previously frozen ultra-small-k compatibility FAIL dominated by numerical time-sampling/interpolation floor, or does a precision-stable non-O(k^2) source residual remain?
guard: This convergence target does not alter, erase, or retroactively relabel the parent confirmatory FAIL. It diagnoses its origin only.

baseline.precision: CLASS defaults used by the parent confirmatory workflow

analysis.direct_quantity: c10_Ccom_direct computed inside CLASS before table interpolation
analysis.smallest_eight_free_intercept_model: C_com=c0+c2*k^2+c4*k^4 fitted on the eight smallest k values
analysis.small_k_floor_metric: median absolute residual of the smallest four C_com values relative to the plateau-model extrapolation
analysis.interpolation_metric: median absolute linear-minus-local-cubic C_com difference on the smallest four

frozen_decision_rule.numerical_floor_supported: at least 3 of 4 core epochs satisfy: tight linear floor <= 0.5*baseline linear floor; tight plateau c2 agrees with historical-ultra plateau c2 within 5%; and either tight cubic floor <= 0.5*tight linear floor or tight interpolation metric >= 0.25*tight linear floor
frozen_decision_rule.precision_stable_physical_residual_suppo: at least 3 of 4 core epochs satisfy: historical-ultra linear floor >= 0.8*baseline floor and tight linear floor >= 0.8*historical-ultra floor; the smallest-eight free intercept has the same sign in historical-ultra and tight, changes by <=20% in magnitude, and its magnitude exceeds 5 times the tight interpolation metric

non_claims: no completed-U1 metric feedback into CLASS
no completed-action spectra or likelihood result
even numerical-floor support would not by itself convert the parent FAIL into a PASS; a separately frozen compatibility rerun would still be required
